#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from LSF
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -g 2 -t 24h --job-name="Train ResNeSt" --output=logs/{{id}}.out --error=logs/{{id}}.err script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from LSF -n 1)
# -n 1         : 1 task (from LSF -n 1)
# -c 1         : 1 core per task (default, not specified in LSF)
# -g 2         : 2 GPUs (from LSF -gpu "num=2")
# -t 24h       : 24 hour walltime (from LSF -W 24:00)
# --job-name="Train ResNeSt" : job name (from LSF -J)
# --output=logs/{{id}}.out : stdout file (from LSF -o, using {{id}} for job ID)
# --error=logs/{{id}}.err : stderr file (from LSF -e, using {{id}} for job ID)
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} for job ID instead of %J

# Original LSF queue: gpua100
# LSF: -q gpua100
# Note: Flux does not have queues in the same way as LSF
# Queue selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling priority depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or GPU types

# Original LSF GPU: num=2
# Flux: -g 2 (specified at submission)

# Original LSF job name: Train ResNeSt
# Flux: --job-name="Train ResNeSt" (specified at submission)

# Original LSF tasks: 1
# Flux: -n 1 (specified at submission)

# Original LSF walltime: 24:00 (24 hours)
# Flux: -t 24h (specified at submission)

# Original LSF memory: 32GB
# LSF: -R "rusage[mem=32GB]"
# Note: Flux memory specification can be added at submission:
# Add to submission command: --setattr=system.memory=32G or --setattr=system.memory=32768M
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory specification, job may get default allocation
# which could be insufficient for this workload (32GB needed)

# Original LSF output: logs/%J.out
# Flux: --output=logs/{{id}}.out (specified at submission)
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} instead of %J for job ID

# Original LSF error: logs/%J.err
# Flux: --error=logs/{{id}}.err (specified at submission)

# Load required modules
module load python3/3.7.10
module load cuda/11.5
module load cudnn
module load ffmpeg

# Install PyTorch and dependencies
pip3 install torch==1.9.1+cu111 torchvision==0.10.1+cu111 torchaudio==0.9.1 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html

echo "Running script..."
make train

# Complete submission command with all options:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -g 2 -t 24h \
#   --job-name="Train ResNeSt" \
#   --output=logs/{{id}}.out \
#   --error=logs/{{id}}.err \
#   --setattr=system.memory=32G \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts LSF directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory specification (32GB) is documented but NOT included in the primary submission command at the top. The complete command at the bottom includes it, but users may miss this. Recommend adding memory to the primary command.
The output/error file paths use 'logs/{{id}}.out' which requires the 'logs/' directory to exist before submission. Consider adding 'mkdir -p logs' to the script.
The 'pip3 install' command installs packages every time the job runs. For production, consider using a virtual environment or installing packages once in a persistent location.
The script uses 'make train' without verifying that a Makefile exists in the working directory. Consider adding error checking.
CUDA 11.5 is loaded but PyTorch is installed for CUDA 11.1 (cu111). This version mismatch may cause compatibility issues.
No validation that the required modules are available before loading them.
The job name 'Train ResNeSt' contains spaces, which requires quotes. This is correctly handled but may cause issues if users copy-paste without quotes.
No specification of cores per GPU. With 2 GPUs and 1 core total, this may create a bottleneck. Consider increasing cores to at least match GPU count (e.g., -c 2 or more).
The 24-hour walltime is quite long. Consider if checkpointing is implemented in case the job doesn't complete.
